# A card released over the Scheduler can change a Board column it never entered

## Problem
In Workstation Planning, drag a Ready card straight down out of the Board. While the pointer is over the Scheduler, move horizontally beneath Done and release. The Board changes the card to Done even though the pointer never entered that column. This matters independently of accepting external bookings.

## Pointer reproduction
Headless Chrome on `514f86fbce`, viewport 1600×1000, Workstation → Planning. Start on `wi-9` (Ready, order 2000). The Board ended at y=620. Move down to a Scheduler resource track at y=740, then across to x=1423 while staying below the Board. Release. One `cardMove` changed the source to Done/order 4000. No Scheduler booking changed. Release directly under Ready instead and its order still changes to 4000. Escape on the same path kept Ready/2000. Reuse the pointer and worker record checks in `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPlanningDeskNL.spec.mjs`.

## Architectural reality
The single-lane `Neo.board.SortZone#getColumnAt` admits a column using its horizontal interval; terminal admission uses the remembered active column. The [Board guide](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/514f86fbce/learn/guides/datahandling/Board.md#L153) describes dragging within or across Board columns and lanes. An off-board release has no Board destination. A second release outside both axes still committed the previously remembered Backlog destination. Fix at the Board so standalone and adjacent-widget consumers agree. A foreign target’s own admission policy is a separate concern.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Releasing over another widget, after leaving the Board before crossing columns, writes no Board status or order and fires no card-move event.
- [ ] Leaving the Board, returning to an eligible Board column, then releasing commits the column actually under the pointer once. Escape and ordinary in-board sorting keep working.
- [ ] A real pointer regression checks both the source record and event count. Include a control for accepted drops on collapsed/empty columns or at an in-board scroll edge.

## Scope
No new drag framework or scheduling API is needed to define the Board’s terminal boundary. This is reproducible on the existing Workstation with no demo changes. Related: #21660. Latest 20 open, open/closed Board/outside-drop searches, recent A2A, own assignments and Memory Core checked November 20; 83 open issues, no equivalent leaf found.
